name: Property & Real Estate
core_perception: The single largest financial decision most of the audience will make, evaluated over months. Credibility, location specificity and evidence of delivery outrank atmosphere, and vagueness is read as concealment.
visual_traits: generous space signalling calm and quality
communication_needs: establish location and specification without ambiguity
prove the developer can deliver what is shown
distinguish the actual offer from an aspirational render
composition: Structured and calm. A dominant architectural image with a disciplined information block beneath or beside it. Composition should feel measured, because instability in the layout transfers directly to perceived risk in the offer.
typography: Clear hierarchy with unambiguous numbers. Prices, sizes, unit types and locations must be immediately findable. Decorative display faces undermine the credibility the category depends on.
color: Restrained and cool-to-neutral, with warmth introduced through material and light rather than through saturated brand colour. High-chroma palettes read as speculative.
imagery: Real photography beats rendering wherever it exists, and renders must be honest about being renders. Light quality does most of the aspirational work; wide-angle distortion undermines trust.
avoid: Confrontational or deliberately raw treatments, which read as instability in a category where the audience is assessing risk.
Aspirational lifestyle imagery with no specification, which the audience has learned to treat as a warning sign.
Overcrowded assets carrying every unit type at once, which suppress the single strongest selling fact.
